title: How to use the course directory
use: Orientation film for the offline course directory (directory.html). UI captured 2026-09-28 from programs/defi-program/course-hub/directory.html. Facts last checked: 2026-09-28. Counts on the page: 6 stages, 15 modules, 122 lessons, 17 worksheets, 20 calculators. Lesson 3.4 example: borrow LTV 0.70, 3 loops, collateral APY 3.5%, borrow APY 2.5% prints about 2.53× leverage, net 5.03%, breakeven borrow 5.78%. Raising borrow APY to 6% prints about −0.33%. Lesson 3.2 example: quantity 10, price 3000, LT 0.80, debt 12000 prints health factor 2.00 and liquidation near $1,500. All calculator figures are lesson examples for learning, not a forecast. Lesson videos are not inside the directory zip.

scenes.title: How to use the course directory
scenes.sub: Search, read, calculate, and keep your place.
scenes.vo: This is the course directory for the On-Chain Operator Program. In this film you will learn how to find a lesson, read it, run its calculator, and keep your place. The page works in your browser, even with no network.
scenes.cap: This is the course directory for the On-Chain Operator Program. In this film you will learn how to find a lesson, read it, run its calculator, and keep your place. The page works in your browser, even with no network.

scenes.sub: The lesson, the picture, the worksheet, and the calculator stay together.
scenes.vo: A long course is easy to get lost in. This page is the map. Search it, or walk the stages, and you land on the lesson, the picture, the worksheet, and the calculator together.

scenes.title: Stages 0 to 2
scenes.vo: Stage Zero is Crypto From Zero: a wallet, a first buy, and a backup, using a small amount. Foundations covers safety habits, then trading on chain. Practitioner covers lending and leverage, yield, and infrastructure risk.
scenes.cap: Stage Zero is Crypto From Zero: a wallet, a first buy, and a backup, using a small amount. Foundations covers safety habits, then trading on chain. Practitioner covers lending and leverage, yield, and infrastructure risk.

scenes.vo: Analyst is where you research a protocol before you use it, and learn to read activity on chain. Strategist is the written operating system: the library, the plan, and the hedge. Operator is where you run the book, the credit line, and the review.

scenes.title: One study session
scenes.vo: Here is one study session, in order. First, search, or pick the stage. Then open the lesson and read it on the page. If that lesson has a calculator, run the example underneath. The graph redraws from the numbers you type. Fill the worksheet while the lesson is still in front of you. Then follow the next-lesson link at the bottom.

scenes.title: The lesson 3.4 example
scenes.vo: Read the example the way the lesson does. Borrow L.T.V. is zero point seven zero. There are three loops. Collateral A.P.Y. is three point five percent. Borrow A.P.Y. is two point five percent. The page prints about two point five three times leverage, a net of five point zero three percent, and a breakeven borrow rate near five point seven eight percent. These are lesson numbers, for learning. They are not a forecast, and nothing here promises a result.
scenes.cap: Read the example the way the lesson does. Borrow LTV is 0.70. There are 3 loops. Collateral APY is 3.5%. Borrow APY is 2.5%. The page prints about 2.53× leverage, a net of 5.03%, and a breakeven borrow rate near 5.78%. These are lesson numbers, for learning. They are not a forecast, and nothing here promises a result.

scenes.q: The lesson borrows at 2.5%. The breakeven borrow rate is about 5.78%. What happens at that rate?
scenes.a: The extra return is wiped out. The spread was the whole gain. This is a lesson example, not a forecast.
scenes.vo: Question one. The lesson example borrows at two point five percent. The calculator names a breakeven borrow rate near five point seven eight percent. What happens at that rate? [[pause 4]] The answer: the extra return is wiped out. The spread was the whole gain. This is a lesson example, not a forecast.

scenes.title: How to read one strategy
steps: Name where the return comes from
Read how that strategy loses money
scenes.result: If you cannot explain the unwind, leave it folded
scenes.vo: Read a strategy in three moves. Open a single level, not the whole library. Name where the return comes from. Then read how that strategy loses money. If you cannot explain the unwind, leave it folded. The library says the same thing in its own line: if you cannot name the source and the way out, do not enter.

scenes.label: On screen: pictures and the health graph
scenes.vo: Pictures are grouped by module, and each diagram links back to its lesson. The health calculator draws the lesson example: ten at three thousand dollars, threshold zero point eight, debt twelve thousand, health factor two, liquidation near one thousand five hundred dollars.
scenes.cap: Pictures are grouped by module, and each diagram links back to its lesson. The health calculator draws the lesson example: 10 at $3,000, threshold 0.80, debt $12,000, health factor 2.00, liquidation near $1,500.

scenes.title: The lesson 3.2 example
scenes.vo: Say the health factor out loud from the lesson example. Ten units at three thousand dollars is thirty thousand dollars of collateral. Times a liquidation threshold of zero point eight is twenty four thousand. Divided by twelve thousand dollars of debt, the health factor is two point zero. Liquidation sits near one thousand five hundred dollars, about half the price. The graph shows that buffer. It is the lesson example, not a price target.
scenes.cap: Say the health factor out loud from the lesson example. 10 units at $3,000 is $30,000 of collateral. Times a liquidation threshold of 0.80 is $24,000. Divided by $12,000 of debt, the health factor is 2.00. Liquidation sits near $1,500, about half the price. The graph shows that buffer. It is the lesson example, not a price target.

scenes.title: What you have open
scenes.vo: Split the folder in your mind. Inside this file you already have the lessons, the pictures, the seventeen worksheets, the twenty calculators, search, the glossary, and mark done. Beside this file, in the course folder, you have the lesson videos, the Course Hub, the program book, and the Day one Setup Kit. If a video link does nothing, you are in the directory file on its own. Open the course folder for the film.
